scenes.raw_text:
INT. HARBORMASTER'S OFFICE - DAY

MARA VOSS, 30s, salt-bitten and unsentimental, slaps a tide chart on the desk. Her uncle TOBIAS VOSS, 60s, doesn't look up from his ledger.

MARA
Three boats out past the shoals last night. None of them fishing.

TOBIAS
You count boats now?

MARA
I count everything. You taught me that.

TOBIAS
I taught you to drive a truck, too, and look how that ended.

MARA
One fence. I haven't touched a wheel since and you know I can't. License is gone for good.

Tobias finally looks up. Closes the ledger.

TOBIAS
Leave it alone, Mara.

EXT. GREYHARBOR DOCKS - NIGHT

Mara walks the planks. EDDA QUINN, 50s, harbor cook, smoking by the gutting tables.

EDDA
Your uncle keeps two sets of numbers. The real one's not in that office.

MARA
You've seen it?

EDDA
I've seen where he goes Thursday nights. The old chapel on the point.

scenes.slug: INT. CHAPEL ON THE POINT - NIGHT
scenes.raw_text:
INT. CHAPEL ON THE POINT - NIGHT

Candle stubs. Tobias kneels at a loose floor stone, slides a LEATHER LEDGER beneath it.

TOBIAS
(to himself)
Forgive me the arithmetic.

EXT. GREYHARBOR DOCKS - NIGHT

Mara finds her brother's skiff, the DANNY-LEE, tied off and empty. A coast guard NOTICE stapled to the mast: MISSING.

MARA
(quiet)
I'll find you, Danny. Whatever it takes.

INT. HARBORMASTER'S OFFICE - NIGHT

Tobias at his desk. The door opens behind him. We don't see who enters.

TOBIAS
You. I told them I needed more time --

A gunshot. Tobias slumps over the ledger of fake numbers. Dead.

scenes.slug: EXT. CHAPEL ON THE POINT - NIGHT
scenes.raw_text:
EXT. CHAPEL ON THE POINT - NIGHT

Flames climb the steeple. The chapel burns to its stones. No one comes to put it out.

FADE OUT.

EXT. GREYHARBOR DOCKS - DAY

Police tape on the harbormaster's door. Mara stares at it. DEPUTY COLE BRANNIGAN, 40s, approaches, hat in hand.

COLE
We're saying robbery. Till was open.

MARA
The till's always open. Nobody steals from a man who knows every hull in the harbor.

COLE
Whoever it was, they didn't find the real ledger. It's still under the chapel floor stone where your uncle hid it.

MARA
How would you know where he hid anything?

Cole stiffens. Tips his hat. Walks off.

scenes.slug: INT. CHAPEL ON THE POINT - DAY
scenes.raw_text:
INT. CHAPEL ON THE POINT - DAY

Mara pries up the loose floor stone. The LEATHER LEDGER, intact. She flips pages: names, weights, payments.

MARA
Forgive me the arithmetic.

INT. HARBORMASTER'S OFFICE - DAY

Mara spreads the ledger pages on the desk. TOBIAS stands at the window, watching the boats.

TOBIAS
Now you've counted everything. Happy?

MARA
Who were you protecting?

TOBIAS
Wrong question. Ask who was protecting me.

EXT. COAST ROAD - DUSK

Mara behind the wheel of Tobias's pickup, driving hard along the cliff road, ledger on the passenger seat.

EXT. EDDA'S SHACK - NIGHT

Edda opens the door before Mara knocks.

EDDA
You found the Thursday numbers.

MARA
Cole knew where they were. Before I did.

EDDA
Then the deputy's name is in that book. Look under the weights nobody could land alone.

Mara opens the ledger under the porch light.

MARA
(reading)
"C.B. -- four hundred, the shoals run."

She looks up. Somewhere out on the water, an engine starts.

FADE OUT.
